To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Bayesian decision support systems can outperform ANNs in terms of accuracy and speed of learning; (2) they are more flexible in the sense that the user can easily change the underlying structure of the model, which is not the case for ANNs, and (3) the Bayesian approach offers a very natural framework for the integration of prior knowledge, which is a key feature of many medical and psychological applications.

1) Bayesian models offer an effective alternative to ANNs in the design of D-SSs; 2) they are particularly suitable for e-learning and interventional e-health; 3) they are highly adaptive; 4) they can be customized to individual users; 5) they are highly flexible in terms of the range of different presentation modes and the different routes through a learning material that can be offered.
Bayesian models can be used to design DSSs that perform as well as ANNs but that are easier to design, implement, and use.
